svg.title: Interdisciplinary future research roadmap
svg.desc: A roadmap from the current stylized benchmark through economics, computer science, behavioral science, and potential real-world evaluation.
svg.text: Future research roadmap: each study resolves a current limitation
Milestones are proposed research gates, not completed collaborations or validated findings.
CURRENT STYLIZED BENCHMARK VERIFIED COMPUTATION
Two operators, exogenous public congestion, independent binary confidentiality costs, M/P/F disclosure, pure BNE, no reporting error or implementation cost.
Current result: Medium congestion has the largest benchmark gap; CCAR improves the benchmark but also has no-effect, multiplicity, excessive-disclosure, and larger-gap regions.
STUDY 1 ECONOMICS
Question
Can a feasible rule induce truthful information quality and
voluntary participation once implementation costs are included?
Method and assumptions
Bayesian mechanism design; participation and incentive
constraints; regulator as a third governance actor.
Potential collaborator type
Mechanism-design or transport-economics researcher.
Success criterion and milestone
Characterize feasible regions; produce one counterexample and
one implementable rule with explicit welfare and burden bounds.
STUDY 2 COMPUTER SCIENCE
Question
Does the mechanism remain safe and computationally useful
with many heterogeneous drones, dynamic demand, and errors?
Algorithm and environment
Dynamic multi-agent simulation; privacy-preserving message
exchange; robust optimization; stress and scalability tests.
Potential collaborator type
Multi-agent systems, air-traffic, or privacy engineer.
Success criterion and milestone
Predefine latency, constraint-violation, welfare-regret, and
privacy metrics; release a reproducible 100-agent benchmark.
STUDY 3 BEHAVIORAL SCIENCE
Question
Do people understand the incentives, and do privacy salience,
fairness, or reciprocity explain deviations from pure BNE?
Experimental design
Preregistered baseline-versus-CCAR choices with comprehension
checks; students first, domain participants only after approval.
Ethics and collaborator type
IRB/ethics review as required; behavioral experimentalist.
Success criterion and milestone
Estimate choice and comprehension differences with uncertainty;
do not generalize student play to drone operators.
POTENTIAL REAL-WORLD EVALUATION CONDITIONAL ON ALL PRIOR GATES
Regulator-supervised pilot with protected safety messaging, audit logs, appeals, calibrated implementation cost, and predeclared stop criteria.
Required evidence: operational reliability, safety, confidentiality burden, distributional access, and public accountability. None is established by the current simulation.
Han Zhang's three-party oversight suggestion enters Study 1 as a regulator/coordinator role; it remains proposed until formally modeled and tested.
